evidence_ledger.title: Complementary activity of tyrosine kinase inhibitors against secondary kit mutations in imatinib-resistant gastrointestinal stromal tumours.
evidence_ledger.finding: Patient-derived GIST models show complementary inhibitor activity across secondary KIT mutations. V654A, T670I and activation-loop variants do not share one sensitivity profile. This supports genotype-resolved screening rather than WT-only ranking.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: Paperclip document metadata; source findings curated against primary publication

evidence_ledger.title: Avapritinib Versus Regorafenib in Locally Advanced Unresectable or Metastatic GI Stromal Tumor: A Randomized, Open-Label Phase III Study.
evidence_ledger.finding: VOYAGER did not demonstrate superior PFS for avapritinib over regorafenib in molecularly unselected third-line or later GIST. This finding is population-specific and does not negate activity in PDGFRA D842V disease.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: Paperclip document metadata; source findings curated against primary publication

evidence_ledger.title: Ripretinib Versus Sunitinib in Patients With Advanced Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor After Treatment With Imatinib (INTRIGUE): A Randomized, Open-Label, Phase III Trial.
evidence_ledger.finding: INTRIGUE did not demonstrate superior PFS for second-line ripretinib over sunitinib. Activity and tolerability findings remain relevant; a missed superiority endpoint is not proof of no activity.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: Paperclip document metadata; source findings curated against primary publication

evidence_ledger.title: Ripretinib versus sunitinib in gastrointestinal stromal tumor: ctDNA biomarker analysis of the phase 3 INTRIGUE trial.
evidence_ledger.finding: Exploratory INTRIGUE ctDNA analyses suggest different relative treatment effects in KIT exon 11 plus 13/14 versus exon 11 plus 17/18 populations. These subgroup results are hypothesis-generating, not a replacement for a prospective genotype-specific trial.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: Paperclip document metadata; source findings curated against primary publication

evidence_ledger.title: Heterogeneity of kinase inhibitor resistance mechanisms in GIST.
evidence_ledger.finding: Different metastases and subclones can harbor different secondary resistance mutations; KIT loss and amplification were also observed. A single mutation model cannot represent every escape mechanism.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: Europe PMC metadata; analyst-reviewed primary publication

evidence_ledger.title: Phase I dose escalation study of NMS-1286937, an orally available Polo-Like Kinase 1 inhibitor, in patients with advanced or metastatic solid tumors.
evidence_ledger.finding: A phase I study of the PLK1 inhibitor NMS-1286937 reported thrombocytopenia and neutropenia as major dose-limiting toxicities. This motivates PLK1 as an anti-target to assess; it does not establish PLK1 as the cause of toxicity for KIT inhibitors.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: Europe PMC metadata; analyst-reviewed primary publication
evidence_ledger.scope: External anti-target background; not a GIST program or evidence of KIT-inhibitor toxicity causality

evidence_ledger.title: Experimental and computational approaches to estimate solubility and permeability in drug discovery and development settings.
evidence_ledger.finding: Physicochemical heuristics identify oral absorption and permeation risk. Treat molecular weight, lipophilicity and hydrogen-bond counts as triage flags rather than universal exclusion rules for kinase inhibitors.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: Europe PMC metadata; analyst-reviewed primary publication

evidence_ledger.title: Association of Combination of Conformation-Specific KIT Inhibitors With Clinical Benefit in Patients With Refractory Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors: A Phase 1b/2a Nonrandomized Clinical Trial.
evidence_ledger.finding: A small nonrandomized phase 1b/2a study investigated conformation-complementary KIT inhibitors PLX9486 and sunitinib in refractory GIST. Combination activity is an experimental clinical observation, not evidence that arbitrary co-dependent targets make effective combinations.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: Europe PMC metadata; analyst-reviewed primary publication

evidence_ledger.title: ADMET-AI: a machine learning ADMET platform for evaluation of large-scale chemical libraries
evidence_ledger.finding: ADMET-AI provides learned ADMET endpoints and computed physicochemical descriptors. Half-life and distribution predictions require particular caution; endpoint predictions do not establish a dose-to-tumor-response PK/PD model.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: Primary methods paper and current model endpoint metadata

evidence_ledger.title: Ptarmigan-1 API reference
evidence_ledger.finding: Only catalog human proteins may be screened through the current API. Engagement probability is a prediction, not IC50; fixed probability cutoffs do not establish binding. Reference proteome off-target predictions are web-app only.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: Official OpenAPI and agent documentation

evidence_ledger.title: DepMap co-dependency scoring
evidence_ledger.finding: DepMap co-dependency is based on Pearson correlation of dependency profiles. Correlation alone does not establish synthetic lethality, resistance causality or clinical combination efficacy.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: Official DepMap community explanation

evidence_ledger.title: Proteome Phenome Atlas
evidence_ledger.finding: Plasma protein associations are distinct from tumor somatic genotype and target-inhibition effects. KIT assay membership must be checked in an identified complete panel table before reporting presence or absence.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: Official atlas

evidence_ledger.title: Effects of CYP3A Inhibition, CYP3A Induction, and Gastric Acid Reduction on the Pharmacokinetics of Ripretinib, a Switch Control KIT Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor.
evidence_ledger.finding: A healthy-participant drug-interaction study measured changes in ripretinib exposure, elimination half-life and apparent clearance with CYP3A inhibition or induction. These are observed, regimen-specific PK results; they cannot be transferred as numerical requirements for another compound.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: Paperclip CLI gateway; full source passage checked locally

evidence_ledger.title: Switch Control Inhibition of KIT and PDGFRA in Patients With Advanced Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor: A Phase I Study of Ripretinib.
evidence_ledger.finding: The phase I ripretinib study reports dose- and time-specific plasma exposure, an active metabolite and a preclinical exposure rationale. Total plasma concentrations do not directly establish unbound tumor exposure or occupancy.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: Paperclip CLI gateway; full source passage checked locally

evidence_ledger.title: Cambridge MedChem Consulting — ADME/T Properties
evidence_ledger.finding: MW and calculated lipophilicity jointly influence developability. The suggested favorable MW/logP region is a heuristic; compounds outside it can still be developable. Early model flags should lead to staged measurements.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: User-specified guidance reviewed 2026-11-14; historical publication date not asserted

evidence_ledger.title: Cambridge MedChem Consulting — Solubility
evidence_ledger.finding: Solubility interpretation depends on dose, pH, formulation and assay method. Poor assay solubility can distort activity and ADME results; kinetic and equilibrium solubility are distinct.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: User-specified guidance reviewed 2026-11-14; historical publication date not asserted

evidence_ledger.title: Cambridge MedChem Consulting — hERG Blockers
evidence_ledger.finding: Assess functional hERG activity against exposure, with attention to free drug and additional cardiac ion channels. A roughly 30-fold hERG IC50/Cmax margin is discussed as a heuristic, not a guarantee of cardiac safety; global predictors can lose external performance.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: User-specified guidance reviewed 2026-11-14; historical publication date not asserted

evidence_ledger.title: Cambridge MedChem Consulting — Predicting Off-target Activity
evidence_ledger.finding: Target profiling requires a distinct model or counter-screen. Predictions depend on annotated activity data and applicability; they can guide follow-up for potential cross-reactivity.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: User-specified guidance reviewed 2026-11-14; historical publication date not asserted

evidence_ledger.title: Cambridge MedChem Consulting — Separation of PK and PD
evidence_ledger.finding: Duration of action may reflect binding residence time or active metabolites. Equilibrium affinity alone cannot determine off-rate; plasma half-life should not be substituted for pharmacodynamic duration.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: User-specified guidance reviewed 2026-11-14; historical publication date not asserted

evidence_ledger.title: Cambridge MedChem Consulting — Kinase Inhibitors
evidence_ledger.finding: Kinase binding depends on conserved catalytic-site features and conformation. Type I and type II binding modes highlight why mutant sequence and conformational context matter.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: User-specified guidance reviewed 2026-11-14; historical publication date not asserted

evidence_ledger.title: Cambridge MedChem Consulting — Lipophilicity
evidence_ledger.finding: Calculated logP methods differ, and logP is distinct from pH-dependent logD. Lipophilicity influences solubility, distribution and off-target liabilities, supporting multi-property assessment rather than a single threshold.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: User-specified guidance reviewed 2026-11-14; historical publication date not asserted

evidence_ledger.title: Efficacy and safety of imatinib mesylate in advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumors.
evidence_ledger.finding: In 147 patients with advanced GIST receiving 400 or 600 mg imatinib daily, 53.7% had a partial response and 27.9% stable disease. Imatinib is the successful efficacy benchmark; acquired resistance is a distinct limitation.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: Primary trial publication, PubMed abstract checked

evidence_ledger.title: Ripretinib in patients with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumours (INVICTUS): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
evidence_ledger.finding: After at least imatinib, sunitinib and regorafenib, median progression-free survival was 6.3 months with ripretinib versus 1.0 with placebo. Its later second-line INTRIGUE superiority endpoint is a separate question.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: Primary trial publication, results checked

evidence_ledger.title: Efficacy and safety of sunitinib in patients with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumour after failure of imatinib: a randomised controlled trial.
evidence_ledger.finding: In 312 randomized patients with imatinib-resistant or intolerant GIST, median time to tumour progression was 27.3 weeks on sunitinib versus 6.4 weeks on placebo.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: Primary trial publication, PubMed abstract checked

evidence_ledger.title: Efficacy and safety of regorafenib for advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumours after failure of imatinib and sunitinib (GRID).
evidence_ledger.finding: In 199 randomized patients after imatinib and sunitinib, median progression-free survival was 4.8 months with regorafenib versus 0.9 with placebo.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: Primary trial publication, results checked

evidence_ledger.title: Evaluation of nilotinib in advanced GIST previously treated with imatinib and sunitinib
evidence_ledger.finding: Nilotinib was tolerated in imatinib- and sunitinib-refractory advanced GIST but did not deliver sufficient clinical benefit to support further development in the unselected refractory population; activity was suggested in an exon 17 subset.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: Paperclip document metadata; curated against primary publication

evidence_ledger.title: Emerging mechanisms of kinase inhibitor escape and clinical implications of ponatinib in advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumor
evidence_ledger.finding: Ponatinib covers the T670I gatekeeper and multiple activation-loop mutants but is resisted by the ATP-pocket V654A mutation. Early 45 mg dosing was limited by significant cardiovascular toxicity; at 30 mg clinical benefit remained limited (approximately 26% at 16 weeks second-line, 33% late-line). Cardiovascular toxicity is the defining concern.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: Paperclip document metadata; curated against primary publication

evidence_ledger.title: Vatalanib for metastatic gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) resistant to imatinib: final results of a phase II study
evidence_ledger.finding: Vatalanib showed activity in imatinib-resistant metastatic GIST in a single-arm phase II study, with clinical benefit in approximately 40% of patients. Development did not progress to a randomised registration trial in GIST.
evidence_ledger.retrieval: Paperclip document metadata; curated against primary publication

results.title: Cogent Biosciences Announces Detailed Clinical Data from PEAK Phase 3 Trial with Bezuclastinib in Combination with Sunitinib in Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors (GIST) at 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting
results.snippet: The most advanced clinical program, bezuclastinib, is a selective tyrosine kinase inhibitor that is designed to potently inhibit the KIT D816V mutation as well as other mutations in KIT exon 17. KIT D816V is responsible for driving systemic mastocytosis, a serious disease caused by unchecked proliferation of mast cells. Exon 17 mutations are also found in patients with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST), a type of cancer with strong dependence on oncogenic KIT signaling.

results.snippet:
The [**FDA has accepted a new drug application for the bezuclastinib and sunitinib combination and granted priority review**](https://www.cancernetwork.com/view/fda-accepts-nda-grants-priority-review-bezuclastinib-sunitinib-pretreated-gist), with a target action date of November 30, 2026.2

Wagner and investigators concluded that the PEAK study represents the first time a combination of inhibitors targeting the same kinase in KIT-mutant GIST has delivered a significant efficacy benefit balanced with a manageable safety profile, and that mutational heterogeneity of resistant GIST is more effectively treated with dual kinase inhibition using bezuclastinib plus sunitinib.
